Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Ibrahim (Abraham), because it includes a detailed account of the story of the Prophet of Allah, Ibrahim (peace be upon him), and the report of his wife and son, and because it contains a detailed exposition and affirmation of what he called to, namely pure monotheism (tawhid) toward Allah, the Lord of the worlds, which is the first thing required of the servants.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Drawing attention to the inimitability of the Qur'an and affirming its high status, and that it was sent down to bring mankind out of the darkness of polytheism (shirk) into the light of monotheism (tawhid), and a warning to those who disbelieve in it, and Allah's favour in making the Qur'an and all the other scriptures be in the tongue of those to whom they were sent down.

• Presenting the example of Musa's mission to Fir'awn (Pharaoh) to reform the condition of the Children of Israel, reminding his people of Allah's blessings, explaining the obligation to give thanks for them, and admonishing them with what befell the earlier nations.

• Establishing the proof of Allah's exclusive divinity through the evidences of His creation, mentioning the Resurrection, warning the disbelievers against being deceived by their leaders and chiefs, and how those leaders will disown them on the Day of Judgement, and describing their condition and the condition of the believers on that Day.

• Explaining the excellence of the word of Islam and the wickedness of the word of disbelief, and expressing astonishment at the state of those who exchanged Allah's blessing for disbelief and led those who followed them into destruction, and contrasting their state with that of the believers, and affirming that the final outcome belongs to the believers who established the law of Allah in this world.

[The Tafsir]

﴿Alif. Lam. Ra.﴾ The discussion of the disjointed letters has already been covered at the beginning of Surah al-Baqarah. ﴿This is a Book We have sent down to you, O Messenger, that you may bring mankind out of misguidance and error into guidance and light, by the permission of their Lord and His enabling them, into Islam, which is the path of Allah, the Mighty, the Praiseworthy in every state; ﴿Allah, to Whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, in creation, dominion and disposal; so He is the One to whom worship must be directed alone.﴾ And those who did not believe in Allah and did not follow His messengers will surely face, on the Day of Resurrection, destruction and severe punishment.﴾

These are the ones who turn away, who do not believe in Allah and do not follow His messengers. They are the ones who prefer the worldly life, which is perishing, and abandon the Hereafter, which is everlasting. They bar people from following the religion of Allah, and they wish for it to be a crooked path so that it accords with their desires. Those described by these attributes are in error far from the truth, distant from every means of guidance.

And We never sent a messenger before you, [O Prophet], except with the language of his people, so that he might make clear to them the law of Allah. Then Allah leaves astray whom He wills, and guides whom He wills to the truth. And He is the Almighty in His dominion, the All-Wise who places matters in their proper places according to wisdom.

This is the commentary on surah 14, verse 5 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar.

And We had already sent Musa (Moses) with Our signs, and We had strengthened him with the miracles that point to the truth of his message, and We commanded him to call his people, the Children of Israel (Bani Isra'il), to faith, so that he might bring them out of misguidance into guidance, and remind them of the blessings of Allah and His retributions in His days. Indeed, in this reminder of them are signs for every patient person (sabbar) who is steadfast in obeying Allah, in refraining from His prohibitions, and in accepting His decrees, and grateful (shakur) to Allah for His blessings, who fulfills the rights of Allah. The two categories were singled out for mention because they are the ones who take lessons from the signs and do not neglect them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 6:

And remember, O Messenger, to your people the story of Musa when he said to the Children of Israel: "Remember the blessing of Allah upon you when He saved you from Fir'awn (Pharaoh) and his followers, who were inflicting upon you the worst torment: they slaughtered your male sons, lest any of them rise to seize the kingdom of Fir'awn, and they kept your women alive for service and humiliation. And in that trial and that deliverance there is a great test to you from your Lord."

And Moses said to them: Remember when your Lord announced with emphatic certainty: If you give thanks for His blessings, He will surely increase you in His bounty, but if you deny the blessings of Allah, His punishment will surely be severe.

Moses said to his people: "If you disbelieve, you and everyone on earth together, it will not harm God in the least. Indeed, God is free of need from His creation, deserving of all praise and commendation, and praiseworthy in every state."

Has there not come to you, O nation of Muhammad, the news of those peoples before you: the people of Noah, the people of Hud, and the people of Salih, and those after them, whose number none knows but Allah? Their messengers came to them with clear proofs, but they bit their hands in rage and disdain, refusing to accept faith, and they said to their messengers: "We do not believe in what you have brought us, and we are indeed in doubt about that to which you invite us, a doubt that gives rise to suspicion."

The messengers said to them: "Is there doubt about God and His worship—alone—when He is the Creator of the heavens and the earth, and the Originator of them from non-existence, without any previous pattern? He calls you to faith so that He may forgive you your past sins of association (shirk), and ward off from you the punishment of annihilation, and postpone your survival in this world until a term He has decreed, which is the end of your lifespans, so that He does not punish you in this world?"

They said to their messengers: "We see you only as human beings like us, your attributes the same as ours. You have no superiority over us that would qualify you to be messengers. You want to turn us away from worshipping what our fathers used to worship of idols and images. So bring us a clear proof that testifies to the truth of what you say."

The Messengers, when they heard what their peoples had said, replied to them: "It is true that we are nothing but human beings like you, as you have said. But God bestows His favor upon whomever He wills of His servants, choosing them for His message. It is not possible for us to bring you a clear proof (burhan mubin) that you have asked for, except by the permission of God and His enabling. And upon God alone let the believers rely in all their affairs."

How could we not put our trust in Allah, when He is the One who guided us to the paths of salvation from His punishment, and granted us success in following the rulings of His religion? We will surely be patient over your harm to us with evil words and other things, and it is upon Allah alone that the believers must rely, both for their victory and for the defeat of their enemies.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 13:

The disbelievers' hearts were constricted by what the messengers had said, so they told them: "We will surely expel you from our land unless you return to our religion." Then God revealed to His messengers that He would destroy the deniers who disbelieved in Him and in His messengers.

And We shall surely give the good end to the messengers and their followers, by settling them in the land of the disbelievers after We destroy them. That destruction is for the disbelievers, and the settling of the believers in their land is a certain matter for whoever fears standing before Me on the Day of Resurrection and dreads My threat and My punishment.

The Messengers turned to their Lord and asked Him for victory over their enemies and for judgment between them. So He answered them, and every arrogant tyrant who refuses the truth and does not submit to it, and does not acknowledge the Oneness of God and sincerely devote worship to Him, was destroyed.
Ahead of this disbeliever is Hell, where he will face its punishment, and he will be given to drink in it the pus and blood that flow from the bodies of the people of the Fire.

The arrogant one tries to swallow the pus, blood, and other things that flow from the people of the Fire, time and again, but he cannot swallow it, because of its filthiness, heat, and bitterness. Rather, he drinks it only after great difficulty, and it tears apart his intestines. The severe punishment comes to him from every kind and from every part of his body. Yet he does not die so that he might find rest, and after this punishment there is another punishment, painful.

The description of the deeds of the disbelievers in this world, such as kindness (al-birr) and maintaining family ties (silat al-arham), is like the description of ashes that the wind has blown upon on a day of violent wind, so it leaves no trace of it. Likewise, they will find none of their deeds of any benefit to them with Allah, for disbelief has annulled them just as the wind carried off the ashes. That striving and working without a foundation is the far-gone misguidance, far from the straight path.

Did you not know, O listener, and the intended meaning is all people, that God created the heavens and the earth in the right manner that indicates His wisdom, and that He did not create them in vain, but rather to use them as evidence of His oneness and the perfection of His power, so that they worship Him alone and do not associate anything with Him? If He wills, He can take you away and bring about a different people who obey God.
And your destruction and the bringing of others in your place are not beyond the power of Allah; rather, that is easy and simple for Him.

And the creatures will have come forth from their graves, and all of them will appear on the Day of Resurrection before Allah, the One, the Subduer; so that He may judge between them. The followers will say to their leaders: "Indeed we were followers of you in the world, obeying your commands. So will you today ward off from us anything of the punishment of Allah, as you used to promise us?" The leaders will say: "Had Allah guided us to faith, we would have guided you to it. But He did not guide us, so we went astray and led you astray. It is the same for us and for you: our weakness in bearing what has befallen us of punishment and in enduring it. So there is no escape for us from the punishment of Allah, and no refuge."

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 22:

And Satan will say, after Allah has decided the matter, judged His creation, and the people of Paradise have entered Paradise and the people of the Fire have entered the Fire: "Indeed, Allah promised you a true promise of resurrection and recompense, and I promised you a false promise, that there is no resurrection and no recompense. So I broke my promise to you. I had no power over you by which I could compel you to follow me, nor did I have any proof. Rather, I called you to disbelief and misguidance, and you followed me. So do not blame me; blame yourselves. The fault is yours. I cannot help you, nor can you help me, against the punishment of Allah. Indeed, I disowned your making me a partner with Allah in obedience during the worldly life." Indeed, the wrongdoers, in their turning away from the truth and their following of falsehood, will have a painful, agonizing punishment.

And those who believed in Allah and His Messenger and did righteous deeds will be admitted into gardens beneath whose trees and palaces rivers flow. They will remain in them forever and never leave them, by the permission of their Lord, His aid and His might. They will be greeted therein with peace from Allah, His angels, and the believers.

Did you not see, O Messenger, how Allah set forth an example: the word of monotheism, "There is no god but Allah," is like a great tree, namely the date palm, whose root is firmly established in the earth, and whose top rises high toward the sky?

The tree gives its fruit at every time that Allah has appointed for its bearing. Likewise, the tree of faith: its root is firmly established in the heart of the believer, in knowledge and conviction, and its branches, which are righteous deeds and praiseworthy character, rise up to Allah, and it receives its reward at every time. Allah sets forth parables for the people so that they may take heed, admonish themselves, and draw lessons.

The example of an evil word, which is the word of disbelief, is like an evil tree, bitter in its fruit and its produce, namely the colocynth (al-Ḥanẓal) tree, which is uprooted from the surface of the earth, because its roots are close to the surface of the ground; it has no firm root and no rising branch. Likewise, the disbeliever has no stability and no good in him, and no righteous deed of his is raised up to Allah.

God keeps firm those who believe with the firm word, which is the testimony that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, and what he brought of the true religion. Allah keeps them firm by it in the life of this world, and at the time of their death with a good ending, and in the grave when the two angels question them, by guiding them to the correct answer. And Allah leaves the wrongdoers astray from what is right, in this world and in the Hereafter. Allah does what He wills: granting success to the people of faith and forsaking the people of disbelief and transgression.

Have you not seen, O listener (the address is general in meaning), the condition of those who denied, from the disbelievers of Quraysh, who chose disbelief in God instead of thanking Him for the blessing of security in the Sacred Sanctuary (al-Haram) and the sending of the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) among them? They brought their followers down to the abode of destruction when they caused them to be brought out to Badr, where they were killed, and their final destination became the abode of ruin (al-bawar), which is Hell. They enter it and suffer its heat, and wretched is the place of settlement that they settle in.

They brought their followers down to the abode of destruction when they caused them to be brought out to Badr, where they were killed, and their final destination became the abode of ruin (al-bawar), which is Hell. They enter it and suffer its heat, and wretched is the place of settlement that they settle in.

This is the commentary on Surah Ibrahim (14), verse 30, from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar (the King Fahd Complex commentary):

And these disbelievers have set up rivals to God, worshipping them alongside Him, in order to turn people away from His religion. Say to them, O Messenger: "Enjoy yourselves in this worldly life, for it is swift to pass away; and indeed your return and your destination is to the torment of Hell."

Say, O Messenger, to My servants who have believed: let them establish the prayer with its due limits, and spend from some of what We have provided them as wealth, in obligatory and recommended acts of good, both secretly and openly, before there comes a Day on which there will be no ransom and no friendship.

Allah, the One who created the heavens and the earth and brought them into being from nothing, sent down rain from the clouds and gave life through it to the earth after its death, and brought forth from it provision for you. He subjected the ships to you so that they might sail on the sea by His command, for your benefit, and He subjected the rivers to you for your irrigation, for the watering of your livestock, your crops, and all your other benefits.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 33:

And Allah made the sun and the moon subservient to you, and they do not cease in their motion, so that your interests may be fulfilled through them. And He made the night subservient to you, so that you may rest and be at ease in it, and the day, so that you may seek His bounty and arrange your livelihoods.

And He gave you of all that you asked of Him. Should you try to count the blessings of Allah upon you, you could never enumerate them or tally them, nor could you ever fulfill their gratitude, because of their abundance and their variety. Indeed, mankind is greatly unjust to himself and greatly ungrateful for the blessings of his Lord.

Recall, O Messenger, when Ibrahim (Abraham) said, supplicating his Lord, after he had settled his son Isma'il (Ishmael) and his mother Hajar (Hagar) in the valley of Makkah: "My Lord, make this city (Makkah) a land of security, where everyone within it is safe, and keep me and my sons far from worshipping idols."

O my Lord, indeed the idols have caused many people to be turned away from the path of truth. Whoever follows me in tawhid (the affirmation of God's oneness) is upon my religion and my way. And whoever opposes me in matters short of shirk (associating partners with God), indeed You are Forgiving of the sins of the sinners, by Your bounty, and Merciful towards them, pardoning whomever of them You will.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 37:

"Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without cultivation, by Your Sacred House, our Lord, that they may establish prayer. So make hearts among people incline towards them, and provide them with fruits, that perhaps they will be grateful."

Note: Surah 14, verse 37 is the verse of Ibrahim (peace be upon him) and the valley of Makkah. The translation below follows the passage as given.

Our Lord, I have settled some of my descendants in a valley without crops or water, beside Your Sacred House, our Lord, so that they may establish prayer properly. So make hearts among Your creation incline towards them and yearn for them, and provide for them from various kinds of fruits in this place, so that they may give thanks for Your great blessings. Then Allah answered his supplication.
Our Lord, You know all that we conceal and all that we reveal. Nothing in the existence, on earth or in heaven, is hidden from the knowledge of Allah.

Ibrahim praises Allah, the Exalted, saying: "All praise is due to Allah, who granted me, in my old age, Isma'il and Ishaq, after my supplication that He grant me righteous offspring. Indeed, my Lord is All-Hearing of supplication, of those who call upon Him, and I called upon Him, and He did not disappoint my hope."
My Lord, make me constant in performing the prayer in its most complete form, and make some of my descendants those who guard it. Our Lord, accept my supplication and accept my worship.

Our Lord, forgive me for what has befallen me of faults from which no human being is free, and forgive my parents (this was before it became clear to him that his father was an enemy of Allah), and forgive all the believers on the Day when people stand up for the reckoning and the recompense.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 14, verse 42:

Do not think, O Messenger, that Allah is unaware of what the wrongdoers do: their denial of you and of other messengers, their harming of the believers, and other sins. He only delays their punishment until a day of severity, when their eyes will stare fixedly and not close, because of the terror of what they see. In this there is consolation for the Messenger of Allah Muhammad (ﷺ).

On the Day when the wrongdoers rise from their graves, hastening to answer the caller to the reckoning, raising their heads, not seeing anything because of the terror of the situation, and their hearts empty, not comprehending anything, due to the abundance of fear and dread at the horror of what they see.

And warn mankind, O Messenger, of the punishment of God on the Day of Resurrection, to whom I have sent you. At that time, those who wronged themselves through disbelief will say: "Our Lord, grant us respite for a short time; we will believe in You and affirm Your messengers." But they will be told in rebuke: "Did you not swear during your lives that there would be no passing away for you from the worldly life to the Hereafter? Why, then, did you not believe in this resurrection?"

You dwelt in the dwellings of the earlier disbelievers who wronged themselves, like the people of Hud and Salih. You knew, from what you saw and were told, what We brought down upon them of destruction, and We set forth examples for you in the Qur'an. Yet you did not take heed?

The polytheists plotted evil against the Messenger ﷺ, by planning to kill him, but their scheming is with Allah, so He encompasses it. Their scheming has turned back upon them, and their scheming was not such that the mountains could be moved by it, nor anything else, owing to its weakness and feebleness. They did not harm Allah in any way; they only harmed themselves.

Therefore do not think, O Messenger, that Allah would break His promise to His messengers, (the promise of) victory for them and the destruction of those who denied them. Indeed, Allah is Mighty; nothing can prevent Him, and He is Avenger against His enemies with the most severe vengeance. And although the address is specifically to the Prophet (ﷺ), it is directed to the entire Ummah.

Divine retribution against His enemies will take place on the Day of Resurrection, the day when this earth will be replaced by another earth, white and pure like silver. Likewise, the heavens will be replaced by others, and all creatures will come forth from their graves alive, standing out in the open for the meeting with Allah, the One, the Subduer, who alone is supreme in His greatness, His names, His attributes, His actions, and His dominion over everything.
And you will see the criminals on the Day of Resurrection bound with shackles, their hands and feet chained together with fetters, while they are in humiliation and disgrace.
Their garments will be of tar, highly flammable, and the Fire will sweep over their faces and burn them.

This is a verse-commentary passage from al-Tafsir al-Muyassar, but the text itself is a brief gloss on Qur'an 14:51, with the Qur'anic quotation embedded in the commentary. Translating it faithfully:

God does that to them as a recompense for what they earned of sins in the world. God repays every person for what they did, whether good or evil. Indeed, God is swift in reckoning.

This Qur'an that We have sent down to you, O Messenger, is a notification and a clear message to mankind, to advise them and warn them, and so that they may be certain that Allah is the one God, and worship Him alone with no partner, and so that people of sound minds may take heed from it.
